heroHeadline: Nakba Day 78: Jerusalem Day Flag March Fills Muslim Quarter With 'Death to Arabs' Chants; Trump Ends Gulf Tour Without Israel Stop; UNSC Debates Ceasefire
heroSubtitle: On the 78th Nakba anniversary (May 15, 2026), tens of thousands of ultranationalist Israelis marched through Jerusalem's Muslim Quarter chanting 'Death to Arabs' and 'May your village burn' in the annual Jerusalem Day Flag March — with National Security Minister Ben-Gvir storming Al-Aqsa and 13 people arrested. Palestinian shops shuttered; Jordan again condemned the march as a 'dangerous provocation.' President Trump concluded his Gulf tour of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE without stopping in Israel — the first such omission since his 2017 trip — amid reports that he didn't want Netanyahu to 'spoil' his Gulf business deals. Trump reiterated his Gaza 'Freedom Zone' plan at the GCC Summit and floated accepting a 20-year suspension of Iran's nuclear program. The UN Security Council held an open debate on consolidating the Gaza ceasefire and halting West Bank settlement escalation, with envoy Mladenov confirming Hamas disarmament is 'not negotiable.' IDF Chief Zamir observed the 'Sulfur and Fire' snap readiness drill on the Jordanian border, citing Oct 7 as proof of the need for zero-warning border defense. The Gaza death toll stands at 72,619+ since October 7, 2023, with 828+ killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, which continues to fray amid disarmament deadlock.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
